comment: Amy, I'm writing because I'm fully disgusted with the level of police service in our district. First, I am a life long supporter of law enforcement; I have first hand knowledge of the career, the lack of support and resources they endure, and the uphill battle trying to get those resources from governments that would rather not support law enforcement (thus their constituents) However, as a tax payer, I am disgusted with the lack of service we receive in this district. I've lived here for two years and never seen a police car in my neighborhood, literally, not once. My vehicles have been broken into, items stolen from my yard, and we've experienced other forms of property crime as well. My neighbors have all experienced similar crimes. We understand that some crimes are less serious than others, but the lack of enforcement in these areas leads to more crime. When the lesser crimes are allowed to go unchecked, criminals see the area as easy prey with no consequence for operating in the area. This has occurred in our district, at least in my area (2100 S near 2300 E). This is not new theory, the Broken Windows theory has long been relevant and holds especially true in this instance. There are people in the area who have had their homes broken into, been robbed in their driveway, cars broken into, graffiti damage, etc. It?s simply unacceptable. As our council representative, we look to you to address this. The danger at this point, in addition to rising crime and crimes becoming more serious, is the lack of confidence that we, taxpayers, have in our elected officials. We see this on a grand scale at the national level, now we are seeing it at the local level, where we once had great confidence in our elected officials. I'm hoping you entered into this field for the right reasons, and still have a strong moral and ethical compass. I'm hoping you will address this issue vigorously and without yield. As it stands right now, I regret moving into Salt Lake City and regularly discourage others from doing so. I'm afraid to leave my wife alone when I have to travel. As a city government, there should be some level of corporate shame that induces our elected officials to act decisively, but all we keep hearing is excuses for the crime and lack of police service. Just two nights ago my neighbor called the police to 2100 S at Wyoming Street to ask for police service due to a wreck near the intersection. She was told that since there was no injuries, and not road blockage, they would not respond and we could file a report online (a vehicle struck her parked vehicle on the road). This left me and my neighbor in the middle of the street sweeping up debris, while others tried to assess damage and move the offending vehicle. Meanwhile, my neighbors wife had to deal with the driver who had no insurance. This is what the police are supposed to do. After two vehicles nearly struck my neighbor and I as we cleaned the street, I called 911 and requested an officer because the situation was dangerous, the driver couldn't produce insurance, another vehicle nearly crashed into the offending vehicle, and there was well over $500 damage. This is what police do, they respond to public safety situations and enforce laws; we don?t leave it up to citizens to address, that's what we pay taxes for. Trust me, people will get to a point where they feel they have to defend and protect themselves, and that can get very dangerous. In fact, there has been talk in this neighborhood of forming an armed neighborhood watch, I'm sure you see where I'm going here?..especially in the current climate. I'm usually the guy who defends police and local officials, but that night, I sat and listened to all my neighbors disparage both because of a lack in service, and unfortunately, I couldn't offer any defense. We are starting to see that we made a mistake moving into the city, but we are not able to sell or move right now. We pay steep housing prices to live in this area, and we pay a hefty tax bill too. We deserve better. My wife and I applaud your work on social issues, but you should know, many people in your district feel underrepresented. At several local social functions, I have heard people comment that you only care to represent those in the LGBT community or those accused of/guilty of/convicted of crime. We are good people that try to be good members of the community and good neighbors to all. We deserve to be represented as well. I'm hoping that you will put your talents to work on this issue as you have with other issues. I'm hoping you will prove the naysayers wrong. We are looking to you for leadership on this issue; funding for OT shifts for patrolman, working out an arrangement with Unified PD, or any other creative solution. This can't stand, it is unacceptable. It needs to be addressed. It's creating a person in me, that is typically a strong supporter of local government, and making me see why people disparage local politicians as do nothing bureaucrats; it's hard to defend when you pay taxes, but you are grossly neglected. Government, at any level, has as its primary duty, a responsibility to protect the citizenry, it goes to the very core of government function??in other words they had one job, and I'm really not seeing that being tended to in this city. Mike Evans 906-241-9048 Sent from Mail <https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=550986> for Windows 10

Subject: (EXTERNAL) Love the new SLC flag Ms. Fowler, My name is Jeffrey Lingen, I'm a member of your district and I'm writing to express my support for the new flag designed for SLC. I hope I'm not too late, as I hear the meeting about it is this evening! I've been following the development of this design, voting on the preliminary designs presented earlier this year, and I was delighted to see the final flag that the committee came up with! I love the way the flag combines intentional symboll'm with a simple design that manages to capture some of the natural beauty of the area. The Sego Lily gives the flag beauty and acknowledges that the valley has a history before and beyond european settlers. White and blue stripes, beyond complementing the coloration of the flower, also call to mind snow, sky, and our lake's salty water. The current flag, with its complicated skyline, strange shapes, and empty symboll'm is completely outclassed by this new design. No resident of our city would fly the old flag, but I find myself excited to fly this new one with an eye towards the future of Salt Lake City. Thank you for your time, Jeffrey Lingen
